Dialogs.NoEncoderAvailableMsg1:
No usable encoder was found. The most likely causes are:
- The encoder plugins are outdated
- A required runtime library is missing

On Windows, check that the Visual C++ Redistributable is installed.
On Debian-based Linux, check that libstdc++ and libgcc are installed.

If the problem continues, reinstall IFME and leave the Plugins folder untouched.

frmOptions.chkMuxMp4EM:
&Empty moov atom
(Writes the header first so playback can start before the whole file has downloaded)
frmOptions.chkMuxMp4FK:
&Fragment at keyframes
(Splits the video at keyframes, which makes seeking quicker)
frmOptions.chkMuxMp4SM:
&Separate moof atom
(Puts metadata ahead of the media data; some streaming servers require this)
frmOptions.chkSkipTest:
&Test each encoder at startup
(Slower to start, but a broken encoder is caught before you use it)

frmImportImageSeq.lblInformation:
Set the frame rate for this image sequence.

You can enter it as:
• A whole number, such as 25
• A decimal, such as 23.976
• A fraction, such as 1/5 for one frame every 5 seconds
